tagline: Two dead ends, joined in 1959, over the pass to Conway.
intro: East of Lincoln the Kancamagus Highway climbs beside the East Branch of the Pemigewasset, then the Hancock Branch. After a run of hairpin turns it tops Kancamagus Pass at 2,855 feet and starts down the Swift River, which keeps it company the rest of the way to Conway. Past the broad Albany Intervale the river slips into a narrow gorge and over two sets of small falls.

The road was two dead ends until August 1959. Pavement followed in 1964, and the plows first came through in the winter of 1966 into 1967. It carries the name of Kancamagus, last sagamore of the Penacook Confederacy, who led his people north in 1691.
season: Fall foliage season. The Forest Service singles it out, and September and October are the popular months for the drive.

moments.title: Kancamagus Pass
moments.text: The height of land comes at the top of the hairpins, 2,855 feet up, with a scenic outlook near the crest.

moments.title: Passaconaway
moments.text: The flat land here, settled about 1790, keeps one 19th-century homestead, the Russell-Colbath House, open now as a Forest Service information center.

moments.title: Albany Covered Bridge
moments.text: A 120-foot covered bridge spans the Swift River just north of the highway, with a campground beside it and displays on how such bridges were built.

practical: Bear Notch Road to Bartlett, the only major crossing, is closed all winter. The highway itself stays open but can close for short spells while crews clear heavy snow.
